case_title: Main Pal v. State of Haryana
neutral_facts: The accused was charged with trespassing into the house of a woman and assaulting her with intent to outrage her modesty. The evidence, however, indicated that the accused had assaulted the woman's daughter-in-law to outrage her modesty. The accused defended himself against the charge of assaulting the woman and focused his cross-examination on proving that he did not assault or outrage the modesty of the woman. The prosecution's case was that the accused had touched and caught the hand of the daughter-in-law and fled when she raised an alarm. The trial court convicted the accused under sections 452 and 354 of the IPC, but the High Court upheld the conviction. The Supreme Court, however, held that the charge was incorrect as it did not mention the daughter-in-law, and the accused was not aware of the charge against her. The Court concluded that the accused was prejudiced by the error in the charge and directed a new trial after framing a charge against the daughter-in-law.
